claim: The General Assembly meets in regular session on the second Monday in January of each odd-numbered year
quote: The General Assembly shall meet in regular session on the second Monday in January of each odd-numbered year to consider any bill or resolution.

claim: A fiscal session limited to appropriation bills meets on the second Monday in February of each even-numbered year
quote: the General Assembly shall meet in fiscal session on the second Monday in February of each even-numbered year to consider only appropriation bills

claim: A regular session lasts sixty days unless extended by two-thirds of each house
quote: A regular biennial session shall not exceed sixty (60) calendar days in duration

claim: During the session the governor has five days, Sundays excepted, to act on a bill
quote: If any bill shall not be returned by the Governor within five days, Sundays excepted, after it shall have been presented to him, the same shall be a law

claim: For bills whose return is prevented by adjournment, the governor has twenty days after adjournment to veto
quote: within twenty days after such adjournment

claim: A referendum petition against an act may be filed up to ninety days after the final adjournment of the session, so acts without an emergency clause usually wait out that period
quote: not later than ninety days after the final adjournment of the session at which such Act was passed

claim: Voters of each municipality and county hold initiative and referendum powers over local legislation
quote: The initiative and referendum powers of the people are hereby further reserved to the legal voters of each municipality and county

claim: The general election is held on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of every even-numbered year
quote: On the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November in every even-numbered year, there shall be held an election in each precinct and ward in this state

claim: County officers are elected at each regular gubernatorial election for four-year terms
quote: at the time of each regular gubernatorial election, shall elect until otherwise provided by law all county officers for the term of four (4) years

claim: Quorum court district and township officers are elected for two-year terms when members of the General Assembly are elected
quote: shall elect each district and township officer for the term of two (2) years

claim: Municipal officials are elected at the November general election
quote: The general election for the election of municipal officials in all cities and incorporated towns shall be held on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November.

claim: Odd-year municipal elections in mayor-council cities of 50,000 or more are abolished
quote: All odd-year elections for municipal officials in the cities of the first class that have a population of fifty thousand (50,000) or more persons

claim: Mayor-council cities of 50,000 or more elect a mayor, city clerk and ward council members in the 1960 cycle (presidential years), four-year terms
quote: In the general election in the year 1960, and every four (4) years thereafter, cities of the first class that have a population of fifty thousand (50,000) persons or more

claim: Mayors of first-class mayor-council cities under 50,000 are elected for four years in the 1970 cycle
quote: on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November of 1970 and every four (4) years thereafter, shall elect a mayor for four (4) years

claim: Mayors of second-class cities are elected for four years in the 1966 cycle
quote: The qualified voters of cities of the second class shall elect a mayor for a term of four (4) years on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November 1966 and every four (4) years thereafter.

claim: Mayors of incorporated towns are elected for four years in the 1966 cycle
quote: The qualified electors in incorporated towns shall elect a mayor for a term of four (4) years on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November 1966 and every four (4) years thereafter.

claim: School board members are elected at the preferential primary election
quote: A district school board member shall be elected at the preferential primary election.

claim: The annual school election is held on the preferential primary date in even years, and in March in odd years
quote: In even-numbered years, on the date of the preferential primary election

claim: Parties nominate through a preferential primary and, if required, a general primary (runoff)
quote: there shall be held a preferential primary election and a general primary election, if required

claim: The preferential primary is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March
quote: The preferential primary election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in March.

claim: The general primary (runoff) is four weeks after the preferential primary
quote: The general primary election shall be held on the Tuesday four (4) weeks following the preferential primary election.

claim: A party nominee needs a majority of the primary vote, or no opponent
quote: shall be certified as having received a majority of the votes cast for the office, or as an unopposed candidate, at a primary election held by the political party

claim: The voter names the party primary at the polls and the choice is marked on the precinct list
quote: the party primary or other election in which the voter chooses to vote

claim: A voter in one party's preferential primary may not vote in another party's general primary
quote: No person shall cast a ballot or vote in the preferential primary of one (1) political party and then cast a ballot or vote in the general primary of another political party in this state

claim: Judges, prosecuting attorneys and school board members are nonpartisan offices
quote: The offices of Justice of the Supreme Court, Judge of the Court of Appeals, circuit judge, district judge, prosecuting attorney, and member of a school district board of directors are nonpartisan offices.

claim: Nonpartisan general elections are held on the preferential primary date
quote: The general elections for nonpartisan offices shall be held on the same date and at the same times and places as provided by law for preferential primary elections.

claim: A voter does not have to take a party ballot to vote in nonpartisan races
quote: A voter shall not be required to vote in a political party

claim: Nonpartisan races need a majority, with a runoff at the November general election
quote: shall be certified to a runoff election, which shall be held on the same date and at the same times and places as the November general election

claim: Circuit and district judges are elected on a nonpartisan basis by majority vote
quote: Circuit Judges and District Judges shall be elected on a nonpartisan basis by a majority of qualified electors voting for such office within the circuit or district which they serve.

claim: Supreme Court justices and Court of Appeals judges are elected on a nonpartisan basis by majority vote
quote: Supreme Court Justices and Court of Appeals Judges shall be elected on a nonpartisan basis by a majority of qualified electors voting for such office.

claim: A mayor-council city or town council may ask the county parties to hold party primaries for municipal offices

claim: Otherwise candidates in mayor-council cities and towns qualify by petition as independents

claim: A candidate defeated in a party primary cannot file as an independent for that office
quote: A person who has been defeated in a party primary shall not file as an independent candidate in the general election for the office for which he or she was defeated in the party primary.

claim: Petitions for ward council candidates may be signed only by voters of the ward
quote: the nominating petitions shall be signed only by qualified electors of the ward

claim: City manager elections are nonpartisan with no party designation on the ballot

claim: City administrator elections are nonpartisan with no party designation on the ballot
quote: All primary, general, and special elections of the mayor and directors shall be nonpartisan, and the ballots shall show no party designation.

claim: County and municipal offices, including justice of the peace, go to a runoff four weeks after the general election when no candidate has a majority
quote: there shall be a runoff general election held in that county or municipality four (4) weeks following the date of the general election

claim: The runoff rule does not cover city manager cities
quote: does not include offices of cities having a city manager form of government

claim: A city manager city that elects its mayor directly may set a winning threshold below fifty percent
quote: may also vote to require that a successful candidate for mayor receive a minimum percentage, less than fifty percent (50%), of the total votes cast for the position of mayor

claim: School board runoffs are held at the November general election
quote: The runoff election shall be held at the same time as the general election.

claim: Ranked choice voting is banned for local, state and federal offices
quote: Ranked choice voting shall not be used to determine the election or nomination of a candidate to any local, state, or federal elective office in this state.

claim: Independents for county, township and district offices file during the party filing period and qualify by petition

claim: Each petition signer must be a registered voter

claim: A person who files for a party nomination cannot be an independent for the same office at that election

claim: The county judge is elected countywide for four years
quote: The judge of the county court shall be elected by the qualified electors of the county for the term of four (4) years.

claim: The county judge presides over the quorum court without a vote but with a veto
quote: shall preside over the Quorum Court without a vote but with the power of veto

claim: The quorum court has nine to fifteen justices of the peace
quote: Quorum Court shall be comprised of fewer than nine (9) justices of the peace, nor comprised of more than fifteen (15) justices of the peace.

claim: Justices of the peace are elected from single-member districts redrawn after each census

claim: Justices of the peace serve two-year terms
quote: shall elect the Justices of the Peace for the term of two years

claim: Each county elects a sheriff, assessor, coroner, treasurer and surveyor for four-year terms

claim: Where a separate tax collector has been created by law, voters elect the collector
quote: If a separate collector of taxes has been created by law for a county, the qualified electors of that county shall elect one (1) collector of taxes for a term of four (4) years

claim: Circuit clerks serve four years; counties over 15,000 people also elect a county clerk
quote: in any county having a population exceeding fifteen thousand (15,000) inhabitants, as shown by the last federal census, there shall be elected a county clerk

claim: Constables are elected by township for two-year terms

claim: Constables are township offices
